evidence: STATIC STRUCTURE (no inversion found in weights/gates/criteria): (1) task/tests/scoring.toml lines 1-11 are byte-identical to the frozen template: gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; floors functional 0.05. score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the template (diff empty). score.py:41-48 zeroes the reward unless both gates pass and functional > 0.05; reward = weighted mean, monotone non-decreasing in every dimension score. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4), so the workbook/skill example of craft out-massing function does not apply. (2) Gates: render (gates/render/judge.toml:23) and constraints (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23) only demand behaviour that is public - sign-in with the seeded password (instruction.md:17, rules 1), a recruiter opening a job with title/team/manager/places and adding a candidate with name/email/source (hireops_rules.md:27-36), Observer reads the board (rules table line 18). No gate demands a hidden behaviour a stronger app could plausibly fail; the only soft spot is 'visible refusal' for a wrong password, which is not stated in the brief but any app that refuses a login inherently shows it - not a credible inversion. (3) Functional criteria: 43 binary rows, total weight 58.5, max single row 2.5 (4.3%); every rubric demand I checked maps to the public rules (drafts rules 168-175, note draft 105-106, live updates/preservation 117-123, undo 96-100, places 63-65, stale 409 77-80, candidate privacy 191-193). Refusal rows are protected by the global positive-control rule (functional/prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'), so a dead app cannot collect negative credit that a working app would lose; nothing rewards a behaviour a conforming app would lack. Polish rows (weights 3/3/2/1.5/2.5) all grade public preservation/draft/session rules and score 0 when the underlying feature is absent (polish/judge.toml:23 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'), so they co-vary with function rather than inverting it. The functional floor at 0.05 requires >2.925 of 58.5 weight, which a create-only gate-passing app with negatives voided by the control rule is unlikely to reach. (4) Known structural trade-off inherent to the mandated profile, not a task defect: a barely-above-floor app (functional 0.06, visual 1.0) scores ~0.236 while a substantially more functional but visually poor app (functional 0.35, visual ~0, polish 0) scores ~0.21. This is a consequence of the template-frozen 0.2 visual weight, which the skill's delivery profile fixes; I record it as a Note-level observation, not a fail. RUNTIME (the reason for Not exercised + risk): raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only entries are scripted golden observations ('Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'). REVIEW_POLICY.md requires hash-bound reward-ordering evidence. The unmeasured inversion risk is concrete: test.sh:224-226 runs the scored suite under timeout 11100 s and, if rewardkit fails or times out, exits leaving the gate-phase reward.json written by score.py with scored_ran=false, i.e. reward 0.0 (score.py:42-48). Functional judge timeout is 9000 s (functional/judge.toml:4, template value, unchanged) for a 13-protocol, 43-row walk with multiple independent contexts, a restart, 120-message thread paging and several 15-second live waits. A strong app that actually supports every flow makes the judge perform every step, whereas a weak app fails fast and short-circuits; if the strong app's walk exceeds the budget it scores 0 while the weak app keeps a partial score - an inversion produced by budget, not by weights. Whether this happens is unmeasured: no full configured judge duration exists for the golden or for any mutated weak app, and no weak/strong ordering run exists. Hashes verified: workspace.cjs 773cc339..., results/workspace.json a848d40d..., frozen solution/app/server.js 4fc5d2c4... all match the index. Timeouts in task.toml (7200 agent, 13200 verifier) and every judge.toml equal the template; I do not recommend changing them without a measured reason.
counterexample: Plausible inversion not yet excluded by measurement: (a) the golden/strong app whose full functional walk (43 rows, protocols S-D, restart, 15 s live waits, 120-message paging) exceeds the 9000 s functional judge / 11100 s scored-suite budget gets reward 0.0 via test.sh:224-226 + score.py:42-48, while a weak app that only passes the gates plus a handful of early rows finishes quickly and earns e.g. 0.6*0.1+0.2*visual > 0. (b) Profile-inherent: functional 0.06 + visual 1.0 (=0.236) outranks functional 0.35 + visual/polish 0 (=0.21).
suggested_fix: Produce hash-bound reward-ordering evidence: a full configured judge run on the golden plus at least two mutated weaker apps (e.g. no live updates; no bulk/undo) recording judge durations and rewards, and confirm golden > weaker with the golden finishing inside the 9000 s/11100 s budgets; if the golden walk does not fit, reduce functional protocol scope (with matching public scope) rather than raising timeouts automatically.
